messages:
jin: FYI seeing ~15% of gpu-attach attempts failing in us-central1 since 09:12 UTC. provisioner logs show 'attach_timeout' and 'ioqueue wait'.
alex: Any recent rolling updates? network or firmware?
maria: we pushed an NVMe firmware batch (1.2.8) to a canary group at 08:50 and flipped a janitor concurrency tweak. could be correlated.
jin: here's iostat from gnode-cc-342 (one of the failing hosts):
```
Device       r/s     w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1      0.0  240.6    0.0 15360    64.0     6.12   25.8  0.10  99.9
```
maria: %util ~100% on the local NVMe, looks like write tail/backpressure from scrub/cleanup jobs.
ajl: @oncall-sre can you confirm if janitor concurrency was ramped during the deploy?
ops-bot: flag-change detected: "janitor.concurrent_per_host" set from 2 -> 8 by infra-deploy at 08:45 UTC.
maria: ok that explains the fsync wave. can we flip it back to 2 on the affected region?
alex: starting a partial rollback: will flip flag to 2 for us-central1 hosts in batches of 20%. running command: `curl -XPOST https://flags.internal/flip -d '{"key":"janitor.concurrent_per_host","value":"2","scope":"us-central1"}'`
jin: patched first 20% -> attach failures dropped from 14.8% -> 2.1% in 6 minutes.
maria: great. mitigation: throttle janitor, mark fw cohort as suspected, and pause further FW rollout.
alex: also routing new GPU autoscale launches to us-west for 30m via routing-policy 'region_pref:us-west,avoid:us-central1'.
jin: capturing metrics: nvme.%util, provisioner.attach_errors, janitor.concurrent_per_host in the incident dashboard.
maria: followups: 1) full audit of FW push; 2) run a scrub-concurrency load test in staging; 3) add an alert when nvme.%util > 85% correlates with attach errors.
alex: created ticket STORAGE-457 with timeline and test plan.
jin: opening incident INC-2026-78 and paging storage owners. tagging logs and sample node dumps.
oncall-sre: acknowledged, looping in storage-team and infra-release. please post exact host list and timestamps. :eyes: :thumbsup:
